$comment: The public surface, classified. Read by scripts/verify-api-stability.mjs, which fails when a
barrel re-exports from a module listed in neither tier — so a new module cannot enter the API
without someone deciding what it promises. A new export inside an already-classified module
inherits that module's tier, which is the right default: adding `getRectArea` to geometry.ts
does not make it experimental.
stable: covered by semver. A breaking change to any of these is called out under a Changed or
Removed heading in CHANGELOG.md.
experimental: may change or be removed in any release. Each entry states which of three
reasons applies, and each reason is a fact about the repo rather than a feeling about the code:
- unobserved: shipped, typechecked, gated, never watched running.
- off-by-default: behind a policy prop no default configuration turns on.
- compositor: reachable only through @hyphened/infinite-canvas/scene, the TypeGPU compositor.
Its pass contract, substrate schema, and shared render pass are new on 2026-09-08 and the
typed command encoder it records into is marked unstable upstream (TypeGPU 0.12).
Purity is NOT a stability reason and size is NOT a stability reason. scene-layer-geometry,
spatial-target, and window-proxy all sound like 3D and are all pure-core roots
(verify-pure-core.mjs proves it) with real consumers, so they are stable.
window-scene-shell and scene-model were both public and both dead on 2026-07-08, and were
unexported that day rather than classified. window-scene-shell exported fifteen names nothing
called; scene-model was a two-line re-export of window-proxy under pre-proxy names nothing
imported. An export nobody uses is not a feature waiting for a consumer, it is a promise
waiting to be broken — and the package has never been published, so unexporting cost nobody
anything. window-scene-shell.ts still exists on disk, since window-proxy calls one function
from it; it is re-exportable in a minor if a consumer ever wants it. That direction is cheap;
the other is not. This is why 'unconsumed' is not one of the reasons above: an unconsumed
export is not classified, it is removed.
typesExperimental: types.ts is a grab-bag — it holds InfiniteCanvasSceneLayerRenderContext next to
InfiniteCanvasRect. Its experimental names are listed one by one and checked to still exist.

experimental.tools: unobserved — the WebMCP tools a store exposes; no product has driven them end to end.
experimental.use-component-palette: unobserved — component insertion and palette interaction hooks.
experimental.schema: unobserved — shared data schemas; runtime behavior has not been exercised.
experimental.diagnostics: off-by-default — this policy exists to switch on the frustum probe layer, and nothing switches it on.
experimental.native-drop: off-by-default — the viewport's native-drag bridge is inert unless a consumer passes `dropPolicy`, deliberately: without one, validation defaults to accepted and `dragover` would have to take the browser's own handling away from canvases that never asked for it. The helper is public for a consumer wiring drops onto a surface the canvas does not own, which nothing does yet. Experimental for a second reason since 2026-08-26: the payload is a union now rather than one shape, and a lane added to it — `text/html`, a dragged colour — widens what an existing `canDrop` is handed.
experimental.rasterization-layer: off-by-default — the policy, scheduler, and snapshot capture ship behind the rasterization prop. P7 intends to rebuild the capture lane on html-in-canvas.
experimental.visibility: off-by-default — reads the store only the frustum probe layer writes, so every reading is null unless /scene is mounted with diagnostics.frustum.
experimental.scene-surface: compositor — the surface contract the /scene entry implements.
experimental.compositor/policy: compositor — which framework passes run and how each is tuned; the field set grows with each shipped pass.
experimental.scene:compositor/policy: compositor — the same policy reached through the /scene entry, which also exports the per-pass defaults.
experimental.scene:compositor/pass: compositor — the pass contract every scene layer builds against.
experimental.scene:compositor/backend/camera: compositor — the camera schema, accessor, and projection functions passes read.
experimental.scene:compositor/backend/surface: compositor — the surface that owns the frame.
experimental.scene:compositor/backend/instances: compositor — instance schema and storage used by scene passes.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/connections: compositor — the edges of the connections slice, one instanced quad each.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/contact-shadow: compositor — the shadow below each window.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/drop-preview: compositor — the ghost rect where a dragged payload will land.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/focus-field: compositor — the attention field around the active window.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/area-light: compositor — the medium lit by each window as a rectangular area light.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/grid: compositor — the grid of the medium, drawn in world space.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/particle-field: compositor — the particle field that drifts toward windows; compute step plus instanced draw.
experimental.scene:compositor/passes/proximity: compositor — the first shipped compute pass with CPU readback.
experimental.window-proximity: compositor — the proximity signal is written only by the compositor's proximity pass, and that pass is off by default because it costs a compute dispatch and a GPU-to-CPU map per frame, so every reading is null until a consumer mounts /scene and opts in with `compositor.proximity`.
